repairVerification.finding: CLAUDE-V7-ADV-1 (my v7 ADV-1) - whenInactive was the one branch not gated on the member's own applicability precondition, so a recovery-typed payload could satisfy an ordinary member's whenInactive
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED - VERIFIED by walking the machine
howIChecked: The fix is inserted as a new first step rather than patched into the branch wording. evaluationOrder gains memberApplicability at position 0 - 'if false, this member yields no branch' - and all three existing branches are re-worded to begin 'true iff the member is applicable AND ...'. appliesTo is widened to require that the member's applicability preconditions hold, and states that a member excluded by kind 'yields NO branch and does not compete'.

A NORMATIVE memberApplicability object states the rule: 'Evaluate the member's selecting preconditions BEFORE any outcome branch. For EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD, payloadKind MUST match the member (ordinary members 0-2; recovery staging member 6). A recovery-typed payload never makes an ordinary member's whenInactive true. A member that fails applicability is treated as if it were not named for this evaluation.'

I verified the member indices in that sentence against the transitions array rather than trusting them. Members 0, 1 and 2 are the EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD members whose guards open 'Payload kind MUST be ordinary', covering ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED, ST-TRUSTED and [ST-EXPIRED, ST-STALE-REVOCATION, ST-QUORUM-LOST] respectively, and each carries whenInactive plus whenActiveSuccess. Member 6 is the branchless recovery member whose guard opens 'Payload kind MUST be recovery', covering [ST-EXPIRED, ST-STALE-REVOCATION, ST-QUORUM-LOST, ST-REVOKED, ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED]. The enumeration is correct.

defaultTransition is updated so the exclusion cannot open a hole: an inapplicable named member now routes to the event fallback rather than nowhere - 'Fallback therefore covers unnamed pairs, inapplicable named members, AND applicable named pairs whose branches/guards are all false.' Without that clause the repair would have created a gap; with it, every (state, kind) pair still resolves.

beforeFallback now states the resulting outcome explicitly, which is what makes the fix auditable: 'A recovery-typed PRESENT while INACTIVE is staged by the applicable recovery member (or PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE if no recovery member applies); it is not ENVELOPE-INACTIVE on an ordinary member.'

The two fixture classes were updated to test the new discipline rather than the old wording. FC-ENVELOPE-INACTIVE now requires that memberApplicability run first and that a recovery-typed PRESENT not take an ordinary member's whenInactive. FC-PAYLOAD-KIND-DISJOINT now requires disjointness 'by memberApplicability, not only by guard text' and adds the TRUSTED + recovery case explicitly.

Notably, /machine/transitions is byte-identical to v7. The repair is entirely in the discipline that reads the transitions, so no state, guard or outcome cell moved - which is the minimal correct shape for this defect.
repairVerification.machineWalk: I enumerated all five EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD members with their states and kinds and walked every combination. The four pairs my v7 advisory named - ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED, ST-EXPIRED, ST-STALE-REVOCATION and ST-QUORUM-LOST - each carry a branched ordinary member (0 or 2) and the branchless recovery member 6. With a recovery payload while INACTIVE, memberApplicability now excludes the ordinary member before branching, so member 6 fires alone and the outcome is a single staging ACCEPT. At ST-TRUSTED only ordinary member 1 names the pair; member 6 does not include ST-TRUSTED and member 18 is ST-RECOVERY only, so a recovery payload there leaves no applicable member and falls to fallbackByEvent[EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD], which I confirmed is refused / PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE. The reverse case is equally coherent: an ordinary payload at ST-RECOVERY fails member 18's kind precondition and takes the same fallback.

advisories.title: memberApplicability's parenthetical enumerates members 0-2 and 6 but omits member 18, the other EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD member carrying a payloadKind precondition
advisories.detail: The NORMATIVE sentence reads 'For EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD, payloadKind MUST match the member (ordinary members 0-2; recovery staging member 6).' I enumerated every EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD member and there are five, not four: member 18 is a second recovery-kind member, guarded 'Payload kind MUST be recovery' and covering ST-RECOVERY, described in its own guard as 'the sole ST-RECOVERY/PRESENT member'. It is unclassified by the parenthetical. No outcome changes, which is why this is advisory: member 18 is branchless, so applicability and guard collapse to the same test for it; no ordinary member names ST-RECOVERY, so it is uncontested; and the operative clause 'payloadKind MUST match the member' is general and reaches it through its own guard text. But a reader implementing the enumeration literally would find one EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD member outside the classification, in the one rule the artifact marks NORMATIVE. Adding 'recovery ST-RECOVERY member 18' to the parenthetical would close it.
